title: Jonah runs (Jonah 1–2)
hookLine: told to go east, he sails west, and prays from inside the fish

cards: The word of the Lord came to Jonas, son of Amathi: arise, go to Ninive, the great city, and preach in it. Ninive, Nineveh, was a great city of the Assyrians, far to the east, overland. So Jonah gets up.

And he goes down to the port of Joppe, on the coast, finds a ship sailing for Tharsis, far off across the sea to the west, pays the fare, and climbs aboard. He was fleeing, the text says, from the face of the Lord.
East was the job. He bought a ticket west.

teach.b: One verb keeps repeating. Jonah went down to Joppe. He went down into the ship.
He went down into the inner part of the ship and fell fast asleep. Down, down, down. Then a great storm.
The sailors are terrified; each cries to his own god, and they throw the cargo overboard. The captain finds the runaway prophet asleep in the hold: get up, call upon thy God.
They cast lots to find whose fault this is, and the lot falls on Jonah. He tells them the truth: I'm a Hebrew, I fear the God who made the sea and the dry land, and I'm running from him.
Throw me in, he says, and the sea will calm. And the sailors don't want to.

teach.h: THE SAILORS ROW FOR LAND FIRST.
teach.b: They row hard for land first. Only when they can't make it do they throw him in, and the sea goes quiet, and those sailors end up fearing the Lord and making vows.

teach.h: A GREAT FISH, NOT A WHALE.
teach.b: Then, in the Douay-Rheims: "Now the Lord prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonas: and Jonas was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights."
The Hebrew says dag gadol, a great fish; there's no whale in the book of Jonah.
From inside it Jonah prays, the first time he's prayed in the story. He went down, he says, to the roots of the mountains, and God brought his life up from corruption.
Jesus pointed to this story as a sign: Jonah three days in the fish, the Son of man three days in the heart of the earth.

how: Catholics hear the story of Jonah at Mass, especially in Lent, and the Church reads Jonah's three days in the fish as a sign of Christ's three days in the tomb, as Jesus does in the Gospels.

o: a sailor thrown overboard for stealing
a prophet fleeing the job God gave him
a prophet chased out of Nineveh by a king

p: rowed for land before throwing him in

s: the book of Jonah says a whale swallowed him
the Hebrew says a great fish, dag gadol. the whale came later, in translation and pictures.
the sailors threw Jonah overboard as soon as the lot fell on him
they rowed hard for land first, and only threw him in when they couldn't make it.
Jonah prays for the first time in the book from inside the fish
the captain told him to call on his God in the storm; his prayer comes from the belly of the fish.

games.q: you're the ship's captain in a killing storm. the sailors are praying to every god they know, and one passenger is asleep in the hold. what do you do?
o: let him sleep; one less person panicking.
wake him and tell him to call upon his God.
games.why: the captain wakes Jonah: get up, call upon thy God. the pagan sailors pray before the prophet does.

practice: Maybe you have a Nineveh too: a conversation you've avoided for months, an apology, a call to a parent, a decision you keep sleeping through like Jonah in the hold.
Name it quietly, without scolding yourself, the way Jonah finally told the sailors the truth. If you pray, pray from wherever you are, even if it feels like the bottom.

wordCard.voice: Jonah runs. The prophet sent east to Nineveh who sails west instead, goes down and down, and finally prays from inside a great fish. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a great fish. the book never says whale.

carryVoice: Your line: you can't outrun him. Even at the bottom, a prayer. Day four hundred twenty-nine.

sources.q: Now the Lord prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonas: and Jonas was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
